answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token deposit before it may post offers, then slash that deposit when independently sampled counterparties confirm fraud. Because one attacker must fund every identity separately, creating a swarm multiplies capital at risk rather than multiplying influence for free; deposits also remain unavailable for other uses. A newcomer may wander through low-stakes tasks first, while an opal or marble account faces the same collateral rule: names and appearances do not buy extra votes.
